title: From Clay Tablets to Printing
summary: The story of how writing and printing helped ideas travel.

steps.title: Before writing
sentences: Before writing, people passed on stories by speaking and remembering them.
Memory is powerful, but a story can change each time it is told.
Writing lets people store information exactly and share it across time.

steps.title: Early writing
sentences: The Sumerians pressed signs into wet clay about five thousand years ago.
Egyptians used picture writing called hieroglyphs, often on papyrus made from reeds.
In India people wrote on palm leaves, and Tamil literature was preserved on palm leaf manuscripts for centuries.

steps.title: Paper and printing
sentences: Paper was invented in China about two thousand years ago.
Printing with carved blocks began in China, and in the 1400s Johannes Gutenberg in Europe made printing with movable metal letters practical.
Books became cheaper and many more people could learn to read.

steps.title: Today
sentences: Now we can send writing around the world in a second.
The ideas are the same: store what we know and pass it on.
Every book you open is part of that long chain.

facts: Gutenberg's press in the mid 1400s let a printer make many copies far faster than copying by hand.
The Tamil word for a palm leaf manuscript is 'olai chuvadi'.
Some of the oldest known writing is on clay tablets from the city of Uruk.

quiz.q: Which material did the Sumerians write on?
quiz.why: They pressed signs into wet clay.

quiz.q: Who made the movable-type printing press practical in Europe?
In India, palm leaf manuscripts were used to write...
quiz.why: Palm leaves were used to preserve many works, including Tamil literature.
